API Inspector Guide 2026: API 510 vs 570 vs 653

The definitive guide to becoming a certified API inspector. An API Inspector is certified by the American Petroleum Institute to perform in-service inspection of pressure equipment, piping, and storage tanks in oil & gas, petrochemical, and chemical facilities. This guide compares API 510 (pressure vessels), API 570 (piping), and API 653 (tanks) side by side — prerequisites, exam prep strategy, career progression, and salary benchmarks.

What Does an API Inspector Do?

API inspectors plan and execute inspection programs for in-service equipment; evaluate condition using NDT methods, visual examination, and thickness data; calculate remaining life and safe operating intervals; assess fitness-for-service per API 579-1/ASME FFS-1; approve repair, alteration, and rerating work; and implement risk-based inspection programs per API RP 580/581.

API 510 vs 570 vs 653 — Side-by-Side Comparison

FactorAPI 510API 570API 653
ScopePressure vessels, heat exchangers, reactorsProcess piping, valves, fittingsAboveground storage tanks
Governing codesASME Section VIII, ASME VASME B31.3, ASME VAPI 650, ASME V, API 651/652
Exam formatOpen-book, 170 questions, 7.75 hours (all three)
Estimated pass rate40–50%45–55%35–45%
Typical USA salary$85,000–$130,000$80,000–$125,000$85,000–$130,000
Validity3 years — renew by exam or Professional Development Hours (PDH)

API 510 is the most widely held certification, covering ASME Section VIII vessel design, corrosion rate and remaining-life calculation, MAWP recalculation, and repair procedures. API 570 covers B31.3 piping, CML selection, minimum thickness, deadlegs, and injection points — piping is the most abundant equipment class in refineries. API 653, generally considered the most technically challenging, covers tank bottoms and floor scanning, shell evaluation, settlement, roofs, and cathodic protection.

Prerequisites & Experience Requirements

EducationRequired inspection experience (last 10 years)
Bachelor's degree in engineering/technology2 years
2-year associate degree/diploma3 years
High school diploma or equivalent5 years

No college degree is required — experience substitutes. Experience must relate to the equipment type of the certification and is verified by employer letters.

12-Week Exam Preparation Strategy

Weeks 1–2 — code acquisition: obtain physical copies of the API code plus referenced ASME/API documents; tab and highlight. Weeks 2–8 — content study: work the Body of Knowledge systematically — design fundamentals, NDE requirements, inspection intervals, repairs, corrosion mechanisms. Weeks 8–11 — practice exams: timed drills (about 2.7 minutes per question) focused on finding answers fast in tabbed books. Weeks 11–12 — final review: weak areas, tab checks, exam logistics. The exam is open book — speed of code navigation, not memorisation, decides the outcome.

Career Path & Salary

Entry NDT technicians ($50K–$70K, years 0–3) build experience toward eligibility. Newly certified API inspectors earn $80K–$120K. Senior/lead inspectors holding all three certifications (the "Triple Crown") reach $100K–$150K. Integrity engineers and consultants (12+ years) exceed $130K, with independent consultants billing $150–$300 per hour. Certification renews every 3 years via re-exam or 12+ PDH credits from conferences, courses, teaching, or technical publication. See the NDT & API inspector salary guide for full market data.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which API certification should I get first?

API 510 or API 570 for most refinery and petrochemical careers — API 510 if your plant is vessel-heavy, API 570 if piping-intensive. API 653 usually comes later unless you work in tank farms. The optimal progression is 510, then 570, then 653; many employers prefer all three.

How hard is the API 510 exam?

Moderately difficult — an estimated 40–50% first-time pass rate. Failures usually stem from slow code-book navigation, weak ASME Section VIII fundamentals, and poor time management. A structured 12-week plan with timed practice exams, or a 5-day intensive prep course, substantially improves your odds.

Can I take API exams without a degree?

Yes. Candidates without a degree qualify with 5 years of relevant inspection experience within the last 10 years; an associate degree reduces this to 3 years and a bachelor's degree to 2 years.

How much does API certification cost?

Total investment — exam fees, code books, and preparatory training — varies by region and scope, and many employers cover it in full. Atlantis NDT provides a tailored prep-course quote within 24 hours; ask about combined multi-certification packages.

What is the difference between an API inspector and a CWI?

A CWI (AWS Certified Welding Inspector) inspects welds during fabrication; an API inspector evaluates equipment in service. They are complementary — senior inspectors often hold both, and API credentials typically command a salary premium over CWI alone.

Are API certifications recognised internationally?

Yes — especially across the Middle East (Saudi Aramco, ADNOC, QatarEnergy require them), India, and Southeast Asia. Europe recognises API for ASME-coded equipment but prefers EN/PED qualifications for European-coded plant. Pairing API with ISO 9712 or PCN NDT certification maximises portability.

Running this as a programme, not a one-off

If you are responsible for an inspection programme rather than a single job, the recurring problem is rarely the code — it is keeping measured thickness, damage-mechanism assignment and next-inspection dates in one defensible place. Asset integrity management software covers how RBI under API 580/581 and fitness-for-service under API 579 behave when they run on measured corrosion rates per CML instead of default rates, and what changes for the integrity team.
